items.title: Inkling 2 Mini makes local reasoning practical
items.oneliner: Thinking Machines shipped a 26.4B looped model that runs near 20GB RAM, pushing serious coding and reasoning local.

items.title: Humans still beat frontier models on basics
items.oneliner: SimpleBench put humans at 83.7% and the top model at 81.9%, exposing basic reasoning gaps benchmarks keep missing.

items.title: Lean verification turns math into software
items.oneliner: A 17 million line Lean proof claims the Riemann Hypothesis, showing formal verification is becoming a serious compute workload.

items.title: GPGME fixed a remote code execution bug
items.oneliner: GPGME patched a double free that can trigger remote code execution from a crafted OpenPGP user ID.

items.title: Android finally retired Binder's C implementation
items.oneliner: After five years, Android removed Binder's C driver for Rust, targeting one of mobile's densest vulnerability surfaces.

items.title: LLMs can now manipulate executables directly
items.oneliner: LLMs reading and writing binaries byte by byte makes reverse engineering easier and malware workflows more automatable.

items.title: Raft implementations needed verification after all
items.oneliner: Antithesis found real bugs while formally checking etcd and HashiCorp Raft, a reminder that proven protocols still fail in code.

items.title: Enroute reworked Git storage for scale
items.oneliner: Enroute says its post-Multi-Raft design can handle 300,000 repositories per cluster, which matters for AI-era code hosting.

items.title: Valkey cut sorted set memory overhead
items.oneliner: Valkey 9.2 replaced skiplists with a B+ tree variant, cutting sorted set memory overhead by up to 43%.

items.title: The AI trade finally looked expensive
items.oneliner: Nasdaq erased its 2026 gains as Anthropic fell 9%, signaling investors now want margins, not just model demos.
